_event_location: Crandon Park Marina, Crandon Boulevard, Key Biscayne, FL
_event_description:
This year is the 40th anniversary of the International Coastal Cleanup, the world's largest, one-day volunteer effort for our oceans and waterways; this is an excellent opportunity to show your commitment to reducing marine debris, along with millions of volunteers from across the globe! Miami-Dade County’s participation, organized by VolunteerCleanup.org, will feature 65+ cleanups all over the county with over 4,000 volunteers. ICC 2025 will also be the launch of Trashathon, a new fundraising concept where the community can make a per-pound pledge to support the overall effort of organizations leading cleanups. Visit HERE to support the ICC2025 Trashathon. If you are unable to help clean up as a volunteer, you can still support the cause by making a pledge or sharing with others.

Join Key Biscayne Community Foundation’s Citizen Science Program,  FillABag, Miami EcoAdventures, and Free Plastic for an impactful and unforgettable mangrove cleanup out of Crandon Marina on Key Biscayne! This will be a guided tour into Biscayne Bay and the mangroves on the northwest side of Key Biscayne to remove marine debris from this vital and hard-to-reach habitat. This cleanup is particularly important as mangroves host many vulnerable species that live within these vital and diverse ecosystems. Our event is funded through a generous grant from the Florida Inland Navigation District. We will have water and snacks, plus some prizes to win after the clean up! For the cleanup, you will need to bring or rent your own paddleboard/kayak, and life vest/personal floatation device. You must sign TWO waivers, please see below!

Kayak/paddle board rentals:  A limited number of tandem (2-person) kayaks, single person kayaks, and paddleboards will be available for rent from PADL. Click HERE (link coming soon) to reserve your watercraft if you do not have your own; prices will vary depending on the type of watercraft you choose (tandem kayaks = $60, single kayaks = $40, paddle boards = $40). All PADL rentals include life jacket, whistle, and delivery/pickup at Crandon Marina. You do not need to change the delivery address, this order link is specific to our cleanup and all watercraft/equipment will be brought to the Crandon Marina. If you wish, you can specify in the Order Notes “This is for the Crandon Marina cleanup on 9/27/2025.” No refunds can be issued for watercraft rentals for cancellations made after 9/25/2025, or for no-shows on the day of the cleanup. The PADL rental link will close at the end of the day 9/25/2025 and the cleanup registration will close by 5:00pm on 9/26/2025.  All participants will be provided:

  • Reusable gloves (if you have your own reusable working or gardening type gloves, bring them as we cannot guarantee we will have your size)
  • Buckets
  • Bags
  • Guidance on the water by a team of experienced local environmentalists

 

Things to remember:

  • Participants should wear sun protective clothing and closed-toed shoes that can get wet.
  • Please bring water in a reusable water bottle and wear reef-safe sunscreen.
  • Download the Ocean Conservancy’s CleanSwell app to participate in the Citizen Science activity to log, tally and measure the impact of your cleanup.
  • Minors aged 9-17 are welcome as long as they are comfortable and can be safe in the water, and are accompanied by a parent or guardian. We can provide Community Service Hours for students upon request.
  • We will also provide data collection cards and a souvenir tote bag with this year’s ICC theme!
  • Download the Ocean Conservancy’s CleanSwell app to participate in the Citizen Science activity to log, tally and measure the impact of your cleanup.

 

Two waivers are required to participate:

  • A paper waiver for Miami-Dade County will be provided on the day of the event.
  • All participants must also fill out the form found HERE -- IF YOU ARE UNDER 18 YEARS OLD AND PARTICIPATING WITHOUT A PARENT OR GUARDIAN, your parent/guardian MUST fill out this waiver in advance.

 

Questions? Please contact Rumya at 305-361-2770 or rumya@keybiscaynefoundation.org.

*Read more about the history and impact of the International Coastal Cleanup HERE.

_event_description:
Do you have a boat and a desire to help clean up Biscayne Bay from derelict fishing gear? Then join us in this year's Derelict Trap Rodeo! During the blue crab, stone crab, and lobster trap season closure, we'll be going out on the water to remove any remaining derelict traps. You can bring family and friends out on your boat to help look for buoys at the surface - they could be derelict traps! This type of cleanup is helpful to reduce the number of traps that are left out at the end of the season. Help us protect these ecologically important species in the bay by removing ghost fishing gear!

We'll be leaving out of Matheson Hammock Park & Marina where you can drop you boat in. Or if want a land-based experience, you can participate in a land-based cleanup around the park!

Everyone will meet at the marina parking lot around 8:00am. If you are dropping your boat in, please plan to get there earlier for parking and securing a spot on the dock to tie up. If you will be driving your boat to the marina, you can park by the gas dock and walk over to the parking lot where we will gather for an orientation. At 8:30am, we will begin orientation where you will get a set of coordinates and instructions on what to look for when out on the water. We will send everyone off at 9:00am and give about three hours for searching and pulling traps. By 12:00pm, plan to be back at the dock for weigh-in of all collected traps and debris.

We will also have an opportunity to win prizes! The boat team with the most weight of debris will win a very special prize and bragging rights! The event will conclude by 1:00pm.

To support this effort in other ways, please consider also becoming a sponsor! If you are interested please visit this link or reach out to friendsofbiscaynebay@gmail.com for more information. 

 

**If you are signed up as a boater, we'll be sending you an email with information about a Captain's Call the night before the event from 6-7pm! If you are unavailable for this meeting, we'll work with you to get you information on what to expect.

_event_title: The Monthly Fort Lauderdale Beach Sweep
_event_location: On the beach at E Las Olas Blvd and A1A
_event_description:
The Fort Lauderdale Beach Sweep takes place every second Saturday of the month from 8 am – 11 am at Las Olas Blvd and A1A.  You can join us any month you like.  If you are part of a group just let us know how many attendees you expect.  For groups we can set up tents and tables.  We provide pickers and buckets for the cleanup.  

We provide Community Service Hours. 

The Fort Lauderdale Beach Sweep together with The City of Fort Lauderdale Neighbor Volunteer Office, and the Rotary Community Corps sponsors this monthly event To Keep Fort Lauderdale Beach Beautiful And Protect The Local Wild Life!

The City of Fort Lauderdale Parks and Recreation Department is doing an awesome job at keeping our beaches in pristine condition. Their equipment does not pick up small items such as cigarette butts, can tabs, and bottle caps.  Volunteers typically collect 100 pounds of trash, 25 pounds of recyclables and 7,000 cigarette butts.  You can help protect our jewel of Fort Lauderdale Beach and local wild life by removing these serious threats to sea gulls, turtles …our beach and ocean environment.

Volunteers meet and register at 300 S Fort Lauderdale Beach Boulevard, where East Las Olas Blvd. meets the beach.  There is volunteer parking at the Las Olas Garage, 200 Las Olas Circle (Las Olas and the east side of the Intracoastal Waterway) ON THE 3rd FLOOR ONLY, UNTIL NOON.  Cars will be ticketed with no recourse if parking instructions are not exactly followed.

Important Volunteer Information:

Please participate responsibly, especially if you have allergies or special needs.

• Proper attire is closed toed shoes and comfortable clothing - things you do not mind getting dirty! 

• Due to the outdoor activity, it is recommended all volunteers wear a hat, sunscreen, and insect repellent, plus bring their own water and snacks. Stay hydrated!

 

• All tools will be provided; but if you feel more comfortable with your own gloves and protective equipment, please bring them.

 

Let us know if you need anything else.
_meeting_spot_details: Register on the beach at E Las Olas Blvd and A1A. Across from the world famous Elbo Room.
_parking_info: Volunteer parking in the Las Olas Garage, until noon, THIRD FLOOR ONLY. 200 Las Olas Circle.

_event_title: The Monthly Fort Lauderdale Beach Sweep
_event_location: On the beach at E Las Olas Blvd and A1A
_event_description:
The Fort Lauderdale Beach Sweep takes place every second Saturday of the month from 8 am – 11 am at Las Olas Blvd and A1A.  You can join us any month you like.  If you are part of a group just let us know how many attendees you expect.   We provide pickers and buckets for the cleanup.  Here is an email template with more information:

We provide Community Service Hours. 

The Fort Lauderdale Beach Sweep together with The City of Fort Lauderdale Neighbor Volunteer Office, and the Rotary Community Corps sponsors this monthly event To Keep Fort Lauderdale Beach Beautiful And Protect The Local Wild Life!

The City of Fort Lauderdale Parks and Recreation Department is doing an awesome job at keeping our beaches in pristine condition. Their equipment does not pick up small items such as cigarette butts, can tabs, and bottle caps.  Volunteers typically collect 100 pounds of trash, 25 pounds of recyclables and 7,000 cigarette butts.  You can help protect our jewel of Fort Lauderdale Beach and local wild life by removing these serious threats to sea gulls, turtles …our beach and ocean environment.

Volunteers meet and register at 300 S Fort Lauderdale Beach Boulevard, where East Las Olas Blvd. meets the beach.  There is volunteer parking at the Las Olas Garage, 200 Las Olas Circle (Las Olas and the east side of the Intracoastal Waterway) ON THE 3rd FLOOR ONLY, UNTIL NOON.  Cars will be ticketed with no recourse if parking instructions are not exactly followed.

Important Volunteer Information:

Please participate responsibly, especially if you have allergies or special needs.

• Proper attire is closed toed shoes and comfortable clothing - things you do not mind getting dirty! 

• Due to the outdoor activity, it is recommended all volunteers wear a hat, sunscreen, and insect repellent, plus bring their own water and snacks. Stay hydrated!

 

• All tools will be provided; but if you feel more comfortable with your own gloves and protective equipment, please bring them.

 

Let us know if you need anything else.

_event_location: Historic Virginia Key Beach Park, Virginia Beach Drive, Miami, FL
_event_description:
Come participate in the International Plastic Pellet Count with United by Blue, Debris Free Oceans, Miami Waterkeeper, and GreenFi.

The International Plastic Pellet Count is a chance for individuals and organizations across the United States, and beyond, to go to their local waterways, look for plastic pellet pollution, and record what they find, so we can all have a better understanding of where this pollution is happening and make the case for action.

All cleanup gear (gloves, pickers, & trash bags) will be provided, but feel free to bring your own gloves if preferred. Please wear comfortable clothing and closed-toed shoes, and don't forget sun protection and rain gear (just in case! ☔️). Lastly, be sure to bring a reusable water bottle to stay hydrated. 💧A water cooler will be available for refills.

Volunteer and join our cleanup crew for a chance to win United by Blue backpacks, bottles, and apparel made out of recycled plastic. We will celebrate our work with free snacks and drinks after the cleanup. Environmental non-profits and government agencies from the Miami area will be tabling to show how you can get more involved in their amazing efforts.

 


A little bit about our partners:

GreenFi is committed to keeping your money away from fossil fuels. With GreenFi you have the option to fund the planting of a tree with every purchase, cash back on sustainable purchases, and carbon offsets for your gas purchases. Learn more and become a member here.

Miami Waterkeeper's mission is to protect South Florida's waters by advocating for resilient solutions grounded in science, rooted in nature, and driven by community.

Debris Free Oceans is a Miami-based organization that inspires local communities to responsibly manage the lifecycle of plastics and waste as part of a global initiative to eradicate marine debris from our beaches, reefs, and oceans.

United by Blue is a mission driven outdoor lifestyle company with a promise to remove one pound of trash from oceans and waterways for every product sold. They have removed over 5.3 MM pounds of trash since 2010.

We cannot wait to sea you at the cleanup!

_event_description:
Join a group of your colleagues for a fun and educational beach cleanup hosted by VolunteerCleanup.org. We’ll help protect our marine environment by removing plastic marine debris while collecting important citizen science data, and compete for the chance to win prizes for whoever finds the strangest thing! VolunteerCleaunp.org will provide all of the supplies for the cleanup (gloves, bags, pickers, buckets, sunscreen, insect repellent, hand-sani) Important Reminders for Volunteers:

  • FOOD/DRINK:  Please bring water in your own reusable water bottles. We will have coolers for cold water refills but do not provide plastic disposable bottled water. Lunch will provided, after the cleanup.
  • ATTIRE: Dress for the weather and wear shoes suitable for walking on the beach. We suggest closed-toed shoes like sneakers or water shoes in case of broken glass or jellyfish on the sand.  Hat and sunglasses are also recommended for a hot and sunny day.
  • FLU and COVID SAFETY:  Follow your company policy.  This will be a socially distanced activity. If you are feeling unwell in any way on the morning of the event, or have had a recent exposure in the days leading up to the cleanup, please stay at home.
  • Download the Clean Swell App to participate in the Citizen Science Data Logging. You will work in teams of 2-3pp
  • Parking passes will be provided for volunteers

  WAIVERS: Registration on Park Link is required by Miami-Dade county parks, prior to beginning volunteer service. This is a two-step process that involves first registering for an account and then clicking the link in Step 2 to register for the activity, "adding to cart" and "checking out"

  • Step 1. Register for a park link account: https://miamidadeparks.com/FL/miami-dade-county-parks-recreation/catalog
  • Step 2. Register for the volunteer activity, a volunteer waiver along with a map and will be provided at this step.
    • https://miamidadeparks.com/FL/miami-dade-county-parks-recreation/catalog?filter=c2VhcmNoPTEzMDIxMjk=

Breakdown of activities for 2-hour cleanup: 

  • Volunteers arrive and check-in (10 min)
  • Introduction and safety briefing (10 min)
  • Explain tasks, distribute supplies (10 min)
  • Shoreline Cleanup, Citizen Science Data logging (1 hour)
  • Regroup at check-in point (30 min)
    • Marine Debris discussion, Q&A, and key takeaways, potential solution
    • Count and weigh the bags to quantify the impact
    • Take Group Photo
    • Award Contest winners

_event_title: SeaKeepers x MORAES Margaret Pace Park Cleanup
_event_location: Margaret Pace Park, North Bayshore Drive, Miami, FL
_event_description:
Come join SeaKeepers and MORAES of South Florida at Margaret Pace Park for a coastal cleanup on Sunday, May 25, from 9am-11am. Weather permitting, we will clean the whole park, including the grass, rocky shoreline, and surrounding streets. This park is located right on the edge of Biscayne Bay, where trash can enter the water, endangering local marine life. 

MORAES of South Florida is an environmental research organization located in Miami, Florida founded with the intent to inspire and retain local marine ecologists. MORAES is committed to the understanding, viability, and protection of our local marine environment through conservation, research and environmental stewardship.

In order to participate in the cleanup, all volunteers must complete the mandatory Liability and Appearance Release Waiver. Waiver completion is a requirement to volunteer with us, and doing the waiver ahead of time will speed the check-in process. 

 

Volunteers should bring:

  • Close toed shoes
  • Sun protective clothing
  • Full reusable water bottle (no single-use plastics please!)
  • Hat and sunglasses
  • Bug spray and sunscreen 

 

We will provide:

  • Gloves 
  • Pickers
  • Buckets
  • Water refills
  • Community Service Hour certificates

 

Please RSVP below to join us! If you have any questions or concerns please contact lillian@seakeepers.org.
_meeting_spot_details: Look for the blue branded SeaKeepers tent and table set up on the North end of the park along the walking path near the basketball courts.
_parking_info: PayByPhone parking is available along N Bayshore Dr as well as the surrounding streets. As space may be limited, we encourage ride sharing if possible and apologize for the inconvenience.

_event_title: Community Action Day @ Fruit & Spice Park (Last Sunday)
_event_location: Fruit & Spice Park, Southwest 187th Avenue, Homestead, FL
_event_description:
Join us on the last Sunday of every month for a day of fun & light gardening at the Fruit & Spice Park! Volunteers will help with weeding the herb & vegetable garden and the more than 150 fruit tree seedlings kept in their tropical climate greenhouse. The herb & vegetable garden features crops like tomatoes and potatoes, lovingly tended by dedicated volunteers and staff. By supporting the garden we ensure there is a space for everyone to benefit from the knowledge imparted by the study of Ethnobotany, how plants and people affect each other!

Responsibilities and Duties:

- Light gardening and mulching
- Removing vines and weeds
- Additional tasks as needed
Qualifications: All ages are welcome. Must be able to bend for extended periods of time and able to work outdoors for up to 3 hours.

Commitment Expected: Please arrive on time and check-in with staff. We recommend having sunscreen & bug spray, a hat & comfortable clothing for warm temperature, and a reusable water bottle.

If you would like to participate in this event, please register on ParkLink in advance.

_event_title: SeaCycle - A Marine Plastics Recycling Community Event
_event_location: Kenneth M Myers Bayside Park - 3465 Main Hwy, Miami, FL 33133
_event_description:
Calling all Ocean Lovers! Please join us at SeaCycle, a special fun-filled community event in Coconut Grove hosted by SeaSweepers, to spotlight the power of marine plastic recycling and sustainable innovation!

SeaCycle is an interactive event where YOU can make a real impact by helping transform previously “unrecyclable” marine plastics into sustainable consumer products. In collaboration with our local non-profit clean-up partners, we’ve already recovered over 4,000 pounds of marine debris from Miami, the Florida Keys, and The Bahamas—keeping plastic out of landfills and incinerators. We are setting up a display of  500+ pounds of marine plastics, including traps and nets, that attendees can compete to sort and clean in teams to win amazing prizes! With your support, this event will be the first step in giving these plastics a second life as useful goods, instead of sending them to the landfill, which is the sad reality for plastics recovered from the ocean. Join us for a fun filled day to learn how marine plastic recycling can be done! 

Event Experiences:
🌎 Meaningful Engagement – Connect with and learn from community leaders and special guest speakers, and network with fellow ocean and sustainability advocates.
🌊 Hands-on Cleanup – Be part of the solution by cleaning ocean plastics to prep them for recycling and transformation into long-term sustainable goods, and win fun prizes doing it! 
♻️ Live Transformation Demos – Get insider access to our groundbreaking recycling process and see plastic waste turn into new products before your eyes.
🎟️ Prizes, Giveaways, Delicious Food & More – Enjoy a day of impact, community, and fun!

Event Schedule: 

1:00pm : EVENT KICKOFF
Arrival, registration, keynote, blockchain based ocean plastic tracking demos, speakers and welcome networking with yummy ocean friendly food & drinks.

1:45pm: CLEAN UP COMPETITION ROUND 1
Clean-up competition round 1 begins! Prizes awarded to teams
 
2:00pm: CLEAN UP COMPETITION ROUND 2
Clean-up competition round 2 begins! Prizes awarded to teams
 
2:15pm: Networking, raffle prizes, food + beverages!

For more info, please check out:

https://www.seasweepers.io/seacycle

ABOUT THE CLEANUP SERIES:

Oceanic Global and Corona are on a mission to clean up 100 beaches and remove 1 million pounds of plastic waste by 2025. Since 2021, Oceanic Global (“the Guiding Partner”) has partnered with Corona USA to host a nationwide series of volunteer Community Cleanups across the country as part of the ‘Protect Our Beaches’ program. Each year the program includes a series of Community Cleanups which are supported by mission-aligned local NGO partners.


PARTNERS

Corona USA is on a mission to clean up 100 beaches and remove 1 million pounds of plastic from their business and beaches by 2025. Corona is our flagship sponsor for the Hub Cleanup series. If you'd like to join other cleanup events to help Corona and Oceanic Global achieve their goal, discover the full 'Protect Our Beaches' cleanup series calendar here.

@coronausa

Oceanic Global reminds us of humanity’s original role in earth’s broader ecosystems and guides us in restoring equilibrium to our blue planet. Our core pillars of focus are designed to deepen humanity’s connection to the ocean as the lifeblood of the earth, provide tangible solutions for resilience, and create a blueprint for coexisting in harmony with our natural world. The 501(c)(3) non-profit sheds light on humanity’s essential relationship to the ocean and empowers individuals, communities, and industries to create positive change for our collective wellbeing.

Founded in 2016, Oceanic Global (OG) reconnects humanity to the ocean as the beating heart of the earth, and provides tangible solutions and blueprints for coexisting in harmony with the natural world. The 501c3 non-profit builds tools, mobilizes communities, and develops educational resources and standards that inspire global action and catalyze cross-sector change.  In 2018, Oceanic Global launched the Blue Standard (Blue), a first-of-its-kind cross industry standard that establishes universal accountability for responsible business leadership, with over 500 + global businesses in 30+ countries and 7 global governments engaged to date. Oceanic Global is based in Brooklyn, New York with international hubs and volunteer bases in New York, London, and Los Angeles. Reflective of its global reach, the organization has additionally been the official non-profit and production contributor to United Nations World Oceans Day since 2019.

@oceanic.global

Clean Miami Beach is dedicated to keeping our community and natural habitats free of garbage and harmful pollutants with a focus on single-use plastics.

The goal is to teach residents, and educate the youth of today, how everyone can reuse, re-purpose, and reduce the consumption of plastic.

By growing the local volunteer community, Clean Miami Beach will provide a clean place for residents, visitors, and a safe environment where our beautiful wildlife can thrive.

Clean Miami Beach seeks to continue providing the Miami-Dade community with: healthy outside activities, ways to connect with nature, stable social interactions, a platform for education, community service hours, and mentorship opportunities.

_event_title: World Water Day: Microplastics Marine Debris Clean-Up
_event_location: Crandon Park, Crandon Boulevard, Key Biscayne, FL
_event_description:
Join Miami Waterkeeper, Debris Free Oceans, PIRG, and Environment Florida for a Microplastic Clean-up at Crandon Park!
Microplastics, tiny pieces of plastic less than 5mm in size, are a major threat to marine life and coastal ecosystems. This is your chance to roll up your sleeves, take action, and learn about the impacts of microplastics while helping remove them from our environment. Join us at Crandon Park and be part of the solution! Together, we can create a cleaner, healthier coastal environment free from the harmful effects of microplastic contamination. Stay tuned to find out how we plan to repurpose the microplastics we collect!

Check out the incredible organizations:
Environment Florida - Environment Florida puts grassroots support behind our research and advocacy for clean air, clean water, clean energy, wildlife and open spaces, and a livable climate.
PIRG - PIRG is an advocate for the public interest. We speak out for the public and stand up to special interests on problems that affect the public's health, safety and wellbeing. 
DFO - Debris Free Oceans is a Miami-based 501(c)3 nonprofit with the mission of empowering local communities to go zero-waste so all can have access to clean oceans and a healthy environment. Since its inception in 2014, DFO has engaged over 12K volunteers in picking up over 64K pounds of trash, educated more than 14K students about marine debris, hosted more than 500 zero waste events, and prevented the use of more than 2M single use plastics through sustainability consulting.


Important Volunteer Information:
The event starts at 9:30 AM. Please be on time, registration begins 30 minutes before the volunteer workday starts. 

Please Bring:

Refillable water bottle. Stay hydrated and be prepared to work outside!
Closed-toe shoes are required and long-sleeved shirts are and long pants are recommended (clothes that can get wet).
A hat, sunblock, and insect repellent (recommended).
Gloves you feel comfortable wearing (otherwise Miami Waterkeeper will provide gloves).
Community service hours are available.

RSVP HERE: https://www.miamiwaterkeeper.org/event-microplastics-marine-debris-clean-up-2025-03-15
Please email erin@miamiwaterkeeper.org if you are having trouble RSVP'ing.

Join a group of your colleagues for a fun and educational beach cleanup hosted by VolunteerCleanup.org! We’ll help protect our marine environment by removing plastic marine debris while collecting important citizen science data, and compete to win prizes for whoever finds the strangest thing!   VolunteerCleaunp.org will provide all of the supplies for the cleanup (gloves, bags, pickers, buckets, sunscreen, insect repellent, hand-sani) Important Reminders for Volunteers:
  • FOOD/DRINK:  Please bring water in your own reusable water bottles. We will have coolers for cold water refills but we do not provide and strongly discoursge plastic disposable bottled water.
  • ATTIRE: Dress for the weather and wear shoes suitable for walking on the beach. We suggest closed-toed shoes like sneakers or water shoes in case of broken glass or jellyfish on the sand.  Hat and sunglasses are also recommended for a hot and sunny day.

  • Volunteers arrive and check-in (10 min)
  • Introduction and safety briefing (10 min)
  • Explain tasks, distribute supplies (10 min)
  • Shoreline Cleanup, Citizen Science Data logging (1 hour)
  • Regroup at check-in point (30 min)
    • Marine Debris discussion, Q&A, and key takeaways, potential solutions
    • Count and weigh the bags to quantify the impact
    • Take Group Photo
    • Award Contest winners!

_event_description:
Join a group of your colleagues, teammates and partners for a fun and educational beach cleanup hosted by VolunteerCleanup.org! We’ll help protect our marine environment by removing plastic marine debris while collecting important citizen science data, and compete for the chance to win prizes for whoever finds the strangest thing! VolunteerCleaunp.org will provide all of the supplies for the cleanup (gloves, bags, pickers, buckets, sunscreen, insect repellent, hand-sani) All guests must RSVP via the Ticket Information tab below. Select your shirt size, as your ticket order. All guests must bring their printed waiver: It's a download in the "additional details" section below Important Reminders for Volunteers:
  • FOOD/DRINK:  Please bring water in your own reusable water bottles. We will have coolers for cold water refills but do not provide plastic disposable bottled water. Light refreshments will also be provided
  • ATTIRE: Dress for the weather and wear shoes suitable for walking on the beach. We suggest closed-toed shoes like sneakers or water shoes in case of broken glass or jellyfish on the sand.  Hat and sunglasses are also recommended for a hot and sunny day.
  • Download the Clean Swell App to participate in the Citizen Science Data Logging. You will work in teams of 2-3ppl if you came with other guests
  • WAIVERS: Volunteers must check-in and sign waivers before you start. Pre-signing the online waiver will help expedite check-in! https://forms.gle/1Xx8yk2Ro59avBySA
  • We’ll be meeting at the White Ibis Pavilion.
Breakdown of activities for 2-hour cleanup: 
  • Volunteers arrive and check-in (10 min)
  • Introduction and safety briefing (10 min)
  • Explain tasks, distribute supplies (10 min)
  • Shoreline Cleanup, Citizen Science Data logging (1 hour)
  • Regroup at check-in point (30 min) Marine Debris discussion, Q&A, and key takeaways, potential solutions
    • Count and weigh the bags to quantify the impact
    • Take Group Photo
    • Award Contest winners!
The park entrance fee will be waived for volunteers.

_event_title: Community Action Day @ Fruit and Spice Park (Last Sunday)
_event_location: Fruit & Spice Park, Southwest 187th Avenue, Homestead, FL
_event_description:
Join us on the last Sunday of every month for a day of fun & light gardening at the Fruit & Spice Park! Volunteers will help with weeding the herb & vegetable garden and the more than 150 fruit tree seedlings kept in their tropical climate greenhouse. The herb & vegetable garden features crops like tomatoes and potatoes, lovingly tended by dedicated volunteers and staff. By supporting the garden we ensure there is a space for everyone to benefit from the knowledge imparted by the study of Ethnobotany, how plants and people affect each other!

Responsibilities and Duties:

- Light gardening and mulching
- Removing vines and weeds
- Additional tasks as needed
Qualifications: All ages are welcome. Must be able to bend for extended periods of time and able to work outdoors for up to 3 hours.

Commitment Expected: Please arrive on time and check-in with staff. We recommend having sunscreen & bug spray, a hat & comfortable clothing for warm temperature, and a reusable water bottle.

If you would like to participate in this event, please register on ParkLink in advance.

_event_location: 2820 McFarlane Road, Miami, FL
_event_description:
🎟️ Please register on Eventbrite! 🎟️

Hey, South Florida singles, are you a baddie in the streets and a neat freak on the beach? Well, now’s your chance to forget the trash in the apps, bars, and clubs, and join other adventurous, environmentally conscious bachelors and bachelorettes in picking up Miami’s mangroves instead.

Debris Free Oceans, a local non-profit organization dedicated to empowering Miami-Dade communities to go zero waste, knows that Miami’s dating scene is tough. That’s why it’s hosting a Red Flag, Green Flag Capture the Flag game and mangrove cleanup this Saturday, February 8 from 3 PM to 6 PM in Peacock Park, located at 2820 McFarlane Rd, Miami, FL 33133.

Singles will begin the program with a mixer among local food and beverage vendors. They will then separate into two teams and play an altered version of a capture the flag game, where they’ll employ their hard-won expertise in differentiating between potential partners’ red and green flags. Throughout the game, players will then work together to clean up as much trash as possible from Peacock Park’s mangrove forest. The team with the largest haul will win a prize, though all are encouraged to stick around afterward for a thoroughly trashy singles mingle. Feeling trashy but not sporty? You can also sign up as a spectator to come and meet some “green flags.”

“We’re so excited to help our fellow Miamians have fun, foster community, make connections, and give them an opportunity to make a meaningful impact on the wellbeing of some of our most important and sensitive natural habitats,” said Caiti Waks, Debris Free Ocean’s Co-Founder and President.

Singles of all ages (21+), genders, and sexual orientations are welcome so long as they’re willing to get the best kind of trashy. 

Get your tickets on Eventbrite! For any questions, please contact hello@debrisfreeoceans.org.

Player ($10) - Allows you to compete in the game, participate in the cleanup, and have a chance to win a limited edition DFO reusable pint. 
Spectator (Free) - Lets you join the cleanup and mingle, but does not include participation in the game

_event_location: 7200 Collins Avenue, Miami Beach, FL
_event_description:
Love the Beach this Valentine's!

Join us on Sunday, February 16, at 10 AM at the 72nd St. Beach entrance for a Community Beach Cleanup in partnership with Burleigh House Condominium and Miami Beach Bandshell. We need your help to keep our beautiful beach and surrounding areas clean!

We'll focus on clearing trash from the beach, the borders of the dunes, the Beachwalk, and nearby community spaces. Our last cleanup at this location resulted in over 300 lbs of trash collected in just a few hours.

Families and Groups are welcome! This is a great opportunity to spend time outdoors while making a positive impact on the environment. We encourage participation from all ages, and it's a perfect activity for kids to learn about the importance of keeping our beaches clean.

Please register for your free tickets in advance so we can ensure we have enough supplies for everyone.

What to Bring: Just bring your enthusiasm and a refillable water bottle—gloves, bags, and cleanup supplies will be provided.

Let’s work together to leave our beach and community cleaner and healthier for everyone!

_event_description:
Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Day of Service at Biscayne National Park

Come out and experience your national park!

Note: *individual* participant must be age 18 and over-no minors will be permitted to participate.

Meet time is at 8:00am, Saturday, February 1st at the Dante Fascell Visitor Center at Biscayne National Park. The address is: 

9700 SW 328th Street, Homestead, FL 33030

What we will be doing:

We will boat across Biscayne Bay (~45 minutes) to the oceanside of Elliott Key. Will anchor in waist-deep water and wade onto the beach. We will perform marine debris removal. You must be comfortable with wading in knee-deep water on soft, mucky bottom.  Once done, we will take photos, weigh the bags of trash, and load the boat. We will dispose of our debris upon our return to Headquarters. Site selection will depend upon weather & water conditions. 

We will provide: 

Life jackets, data sheets, trash bags, bug spray, sunscreen, first-aid kit, gloves for hand protection (however, these are a one-size-fits-all deal, so if you have your own that you prefer, like garden or work gloves, please feel free to bring those), trash grabbers, your own trash collection buckets if you so desire.

Please bring: 

Close-toed shoes that can get wet are mandatory-this is a safety requirement. (dive booties are recommended), bathing suit, clothing that can get wet. Hat, sunglasses, water jugs and water bottles (bring already full if possible), snacks if you want. 

For more information, contact Ana Zangroniz at: azangroniz@ufl.edu. 

This event is to honor the legacy and memory of Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. This event is a partnership between Biscayne National Park and the Florida Sea Grant Extension Program in Miami-Dade County.

_event_description:
Saturday, January 18, 2025 @ 9:30am-12:30pm

IMPORTANT: To participate, you must both fill out the waiver (link below) AND register for a ticket on this page.

Join Key Biscayne Community Foundation’s Citizen Science Program,  FillABag, Miami EcoAdventures, and Free Plastic for an impactful and unforgettable mangrove cleanup in the Bear Cut Preserve in Key Biscayne! This will be a guided tour into Biscayne Bay and the mangroves to remove marine debris from this vital and hard-to-reach habitat. This cleanup is particularly important as mangroves host many vulnerable species that live within these vital and diverse ecosystems, and the recent storms have likely added more debris to this area. There is also a walking portion for those who do not wish to be in the water; however, keep in mind this may be difficult as you will be climbing through the trees and there are no defined trails. Please keep in mind, EVERY MEMBER OF YOUR PARTY must be registered (Parents, if you are attending with your child, you must also be registered and fill out the waiver).

Our event is funded through a generous grant from the Florida Inland Navigation District. We will have water and snacks, plus some prizes to win after the clean up! For the water portion of the cleanup, you will need to bring or rent your own paddleboard/kayak, and life vest/personal floatation device.

Kayak/paddle board rentals:  A limited number of tandem (2-person) kayaks and paddleboards will be available for rent from PADL. Click here to reserve a rented watercraft if you do not have your own; prices will vary depending on the type of watercraft you choose (single kayaks = $40 and tandem kayaks = $60). All PADL rentals include life jacket, whistle, and delivery/pickup. You do not need to change the delivery address, this order link is specific to our cleanup and all watercraft/equipment will be brought to our launch point near the Crandon Marina (the star on the map below, click on the map to enlarge it). No refunds can be issued for watercraft rentals for cancellations made after 01/16/2025 or for no-shows on the day of the cleanup. The PADL rental link will close at the end of the day 01/16/2025 and the cleanup registration will close by 5:00pm on 01/17/2025. 

All participants will be provided:

  • reusable gloves (if you have your own reusable working or gardening type gloves, bring them as we cannot guarantee we will have your size)
  • buckets
  • bags
  • guidance on the water by a team of experienced local environmentalists

 

Participants should wear sun protective clothing and closed-toed shoes that can get wet. Please bring water in a reusable water bottle and wear reef-safe sunscreen. Download the Ocean Conservancy’s CleanSwell app to participate in the Citizen Science activity to log, tally and measure the impact of your cleanup.

Minors aged 9-17 are welcome as long as they are comfortable and can be safe in the water, and are accompanied by a parent or guardian. We can provide Community Service Hours for students upon request. You will get a maximum of 3 hours for this cleanup.

Waivers are required to participate:

  • Waivers are available at this LINK. FILLING OUT THE WAIVER DOES NOT REGISTER YOU FOR THE EVENT, PLEASE ALSO REGISTER BELOW.
    If you are under 18 and coming without a parent or guardian, you must have a parent/guardian print and sign the waiver in advance and you MUST have your guardian fill out the waiver on your behalf.
  • Paper waivers will be provided the day of the event if you forget to sign online, however we prefer to keep our printing to a minimum.  Therefore, filling out the waiver online is preferrable.

Questions? Please contact Rumya at 305-361-2770 or rumya@keybiscaynefoundation.org

On the third Saturday of every month, volunteers can assist the Causeway staff beautify this coastal park and keep our ocean ecosystem healthy. Gloves and trash bags will be provided, but volunteers are encouraged to bring their own reusable gloves to reduce waste.  

This opportunity is made possible with the support of Mandarin Oriental Hotel Group. Mandarin Oriental Hotel Group is committed to contributing to the communities in which they operate and responsibly managing their environmental impacts and social commitments. One of their guiding principles at Mandarin Oriental is ‘Acting with responsibility’, which they strive to achieve through their “Naturally Better” program.

Responsibilities and Duties:

- Removing microplastics and trash along the Virginia Key South (across from MAST Academy) shoreline
- Additional tasks as needed
Qualifications: Youth under 15 must have a parent/guardian present.

All ages welcome.

_event_title: Community Action Day @ Deering Estate (2nd Saturday)
_event_location: Deering Estate, Southwest 72nd Avenue, Miami, FL
_event_description:
Volunteers are needed to help achieve Deering Estate's conservation and restoration goals. Our team of professional naturalists will guide volunteers through various projects.

Responsibilities and Duties:

- Removing invasive plants
- Planting native species
- Mulching
- Cleaning up litter
Qualifications: Must be able to work outdoors in Florida heat/humidity.

Commitment Expected: Please arrive a few minutes early in order to check-in. Volunteers will be working in partially forested areas; closed toe shoes, long sleeve shirts, long pants, reusable water bottle are required. We will provide gloves, water cooler, and receptacles to place removed trash or plant material.

Community service hours letters will be emailed, by request, following the event.

If you would like participate in this event, please register on ParkLink in advance.

_event_location: Haulover Park, Collins Avenue, Miami Beach, FL
_event_description:
On the first Saturday of every month, volunteers can assist the Haulover Park staff and beautify this coastal park to keep our ocean ecosystem healthy. Volunteers will also get an opportunity to learn about their impact on local wildlife.

This volunteer opportunity is made possible with the support of our community partner, Miami-Dade County Sea Turtle Conservation Program (STCP). The STCP works to protect our sea turtle nests on 19 miles of Miami beaches during nesting season (March-October). STCP is committed to protecting our coastal and ocean ecosystems year-round, and educating the public on best conservation practices. Join STCP team members at our monthly coastal cleanups to learn more about the endangered sea turtle species that utilize our local ecosystems.

Responsibilities and Duties:

- Removing microplastics and trash
- Additional tasks as needed
Qualifications: Youth under 15 must have a parent/guardian present.

Commitment Expected: Please arrive at your scheduled start time and check-in with Sea Turtle staff. Please bring a refillable water bottle, closed-toed shoes, and protection from the sun (sunscreen, hats, sunglasses). Please register on ParkLink in advance.

_event_description:
Monday, December 30, 2024 @ 10:00am-1:00pm

Join Key Biscayne Community Foundation’s Citizen Science Program,  FillABag, Miami EcoAdventures, and Free Plastic for an impactful and unforgettable mangrove cleanup in Bill Baggs Cape Florida Park in Key Biscayne! This will be a guided tour into Biscayne Bay and the mangroves to remove marine debris from this vital and hard-to-reach habitat. This cleanup is particularly important as mangroves host many vulnerable species that live within these vital and diverse ecosystems, and the recent storms have likely added more debris to this area. There is also a walking portion for those who do not wish to be in the water, which includes several trails into the beautiful nature of Bill Baggs.

Our event is funded through a generous grant from the Florida Inland Navigation District. We will have water and snacks, plus some prizes to win after the clean up! For the cleanup, you will need to bring or rent your own paddleboard/kayak, and life vest/personal floatation device.

Kayak/paddle board rentals:  A limited number of tandem (2-person) kayaks and paddleboards will be available for rent from PADL. Click here to reserve a rented watercraft if you do not have your own; prices will vary depending on the type of watercraft you choose (single kayaks = $40, tandem kayaks = $60, paddle boards = $40). All PADL rentals include life jacket, whistle, and delivery/pickup. You do not need to change the delivery address, this order link is specific to our cleanup and all watercraft/equipment will be brought to the parking area at No Name Harbor in Bill Baggs. No refunds can be issued for watercraft rentals for cancellations made after 12/28/2024 or for no-shows on the day of the cleanup. The PADL rental link will close at the end of the day 12/28/2024 and the cleanup registration will close by 5:00pm on 12/29/2024. 

All participants will be provided:

  • reusable gloves (if you have your own reusable working or gardening type gloves, bring them as we cannot guarantee we will have your size)
  • buckets
  • bags
  • guidance on the water by a team of experienced local environmentalists
     

Participants should wear sun protective clothing and closed-toed shoes that can get wet. Please bring water in a reusable water bottle and wear reef-safe sunscreen. Download the Ocean Conservancy’s CleanSwell app to participate in the Citizen Science activity to log, tally and measure the impact of your cleanup.

Minors aged 9-17 are welcome as long as they are comfortable and can be safe in the water, and are accompanied by a parent or guardian. We can provide Community Service Hours for students upon request. You will get a maximum of 3 hours for this cleanup.

Waivers are required to participate:

  • Waivers are available at this LINK. FILLING OUT THE WAIVER DOES NOT REGISTER YOU FOR THE EVENT, PLEASE ALSO REGISTER BELOW.
  • If you are under 18 and coming without a parent or guardian, you must have a parent/guardian print and sign the waiver HERE in advance. You MUST have your guardian fill out the waiver on your behalf.
  • Paper waivers will be provided the day of the event in the event you forget to sign online, however we prefer to keep our printing to a minimum.  Therefore, filling out the waiver online is preferrable.
     

Questions? Please contact Rumya at 305-361-2770 or rumya@keybiscaynefoundation.org.

Join SeaKeepers to celebrate the holidays at Margaret Pace Park on Saturday, December 21, 2024! Along with a coastal cleanup to give back to our ocean, celebrate the season of giving and reduce waste by bringing in an unwrapped toy to be donated to a child through the Marine Toys for Tots program!

Close-toe shoes
Comfortable clothes that may get dirty
Water in a REUSABLE water bottle (no plastic please!)
Sunscreen and bug spray if needed
Hat and sunglasses if wanted

Buckets
Reusable mesh bags
Gloves
Water refills
Community service hours

Join Miami EcoAdventures & local non-profit Debris Free Oceans for our monthly Citizen Science Project Activity, hosted at Crandon Park every 2nd Saturday. Citizen Science is a way for the general public to be directly involved in the process of scientific data collection and to be engaged in scientific thinking. The goal of this activity is to have volunteers become amateur scientists while working with a group of professional scientists to collect critical data on marine debris in our local environment. 

Responsibilities and Duties:

Cleaning up the beach
Sorting marine debris collected
Gathering and recording data
Qualifications: Volunteers under 13 must participate with a parent/guardian present. Please bring a refillable water bottle, closed-toed shoes, and protection from the sun (sunscreen, hats, sunglasses).

Commitment Expected: Please arrive at your scheduled start time and we recommend staying for the duration of the activity. Community service hours will be provided via email following the event.

_event_description:
SATURDAY, November 23, 2024 @ 9:00am-12:00pm

Join Key Biscayne Community Foundation’s Citizen Science Program,  FillABag, Miami EcoAdventures, and Free Plastic for an impactful and unforgettable mangrove cleanup in Peacock Park in Coconut Grove! This will be a guided tour into Biscayne Bay and the mangroves to remove marine debris from this vital and hard-to-reach habitat. This cleanup is particularly important as mangroves host many vulnerable species that live within these vital and diverse ecosystems, and the recent storms have likely added more debris to this area.

Our event is funded through a generous grant from the Florida Inland Navigation District. We will have water and snacks, plus some prizes to win after the clean up! For the cleanup, you will need to bring or rent your own paddleboard/kayak, and life vest/personal floatation device.

Kayak/paddle board rentals:  A limited number of tandem (2-person) kayaks and paddleboards will be available for rent from PADL. Click here to reserve a rented watercraft if you do not have your own; prices will vary depending on the type of watercraft you choose (tandem kayaks = $60, paddle boards = $40). All PADL rentals include life jacket, whistle, and delivery/pickup. You do not need to change the delivery address, this order link is specific to our cleanup and all watercraft/equipment will be brought to the parking area where we will enter West Point Preserve. No refunds can be issued for watercraft rentals for cancellations made after 10/24/2024 or for no-shows on the day of the cleanup. The PADL rental link will close at the end of the day 10/24/2024 and the cleanup registration will close by 5:00pm on 10/25/2024. 

All participants will be provided:

  • reusable gloves (if you have your own reusable working or gardening type gloves, bring them as we cannot guarantee we will have your size)
  • buckets
  • bags
  • guidance on the water by a team of experienced local environmentalists

 

Participants should wear sun protective clothing and closed-toed shoes that can get wet. Please bring water in a reusable water bottle and wear reef-safe sunscreen. Download the Ocean Conservancy’s CleanSwell app to participate in the Citizen Science activity to log, tally and measure the impact of your cleanup.

Minors aged 9-17 are welcome as long as they are comfortable and can be safe in the water, and are accompanied by a parent or guardian. We can provide Community Service Hours for students upon request. You will get a maximum of 3 hours for this cleanup.

Waivers are required to participate:

  • Waivers are available at this LINK. FILLING OUT THE WAIVER DOES NOT REGISTER YOU FOR THE EVENT, PLEASE ALSO REGISTER BELOW.
  • If you are under 18 and coming without a parent or guardian, you must have a parent/guardian print and sign the waiver HERE in advance. You MUST have your guardian fill out the waiver on your behalf.
  • Paper waivers will be provided the day of the event in the event you forget to sign online, however we prefer to keep our printing to a minimum.  Therefore, filling out the waiver online is preferrable.

 

Questions? Please contact Rumya at 305-361-2770 or rumya@keybiscaynefoundation.org.

_event_title: Keep it Clean: Mowry Canal Cleanup for National Public Lands Day
_event_location: Dante Fascell Visitor Center, Southwest 328th Street, Homestead, FL
_event_description:
Keep it Clean: Mowry Canal Cleanup for National Public Lands Day

Join us for a fulfilling day of environmental stewardship at Biscayne National Park as we celebrate National Public Lands Day with the Mowry Canal Cleanup on Saturday, September 28th, from 8 AM to 12 PM. This event offers a unique opportunity to make a positive impact on our local environment by removing debris from the park’s lands and waterways.

  • Land-Based Cleanup (8 AM - 12 PM): Open to all ages, this effort will focus on cleaning up the land around the Mowry Canal. Volunteers will work alongside park staff and community members to help preserve the beauty and health of Biscayne’s terrestrial areas.
  • Paddle Cleanup (10 AM - 12 PM): A canoe-based cleanup led by park rangers. This portion of the event is limited to 10 participants, and all paddlers must be 11 years or older. Experienced paddlers should be comfortable in the water and able to endure strenuous activity. Participants under 18 must be accompanied by a guardian.
     

This collaborative effort aims to enhance the habitat for local wildlife and improve water quality, ensuring Biscayne remains a pristine sanctuary for visitors and wildlife alike. Volunteers of all ages are welcome, and no prior experience is necessary. We’ll provide all necessary cleanup supplies, including gloves, bags, and safety equipment.

Wear comfortable clothing, closed-toe shoes, and bring a reusable water bottle. The day promises to be both rewarding and educational, offering insight into the challenges our marine environments face and how collective efforts can help protect them.

_event_location: SW 87th Ave & Southwest 212th Street, Cutler Bay, FL
_event_description:
The Town of Cutler Bay invites you to participate in the International Coastal Cleanup Day 2024! We'll remove debris and litter from the area, helping protect our environment and waterways. Bring your friends and family, and let's make a positive impact together.

Note: Meetup location is at the corner of SW 87th Ave and SW 212th Street. Volunteers can park at Cutler Bay Senior High School (8601 SW 212th St, Cutler Bay, FL 33189).

We will provide garbage bags, gloves, data collection cards, and a souvenir tote bag with this year’s marine animal theme, penguins!  *Community Service hours also provided. Registration + waivers are required to participate.*

  • You can complete the online waivers in advance to help expedite check-in on the day of.
  • However, if you are under 18 and coming without a parent or guardian, you must have a parent/guardian print and sign the waiver HERE in advance, and bring it with you to the cleanup.

This year’s Penguin T-Shirts are available for purchase here: www.bonfire.com/miami-icc-2024. Order before August 30 if you want to guarantee your shirt arrives before the cleanup.

Important details:
  • Download the Ocean Conservancy’s CleanSwell app to participate in the Citizen Science activity to log, tally and measure the impact of your cleanup.  It is easier and more fun than using paper data cards!
  • Dress for the weather and wear appropriate footwear.
  • Sunglasses, hat, sweat towel, and bug spray are recommended.
  • If you have your own reusable working or gardening type gloves, bring them. We will be providing gloves but cannot guarantee they will be in your size.
  • Please bring water in a reusable container. Let’s reduce waste and refuse single-use disposable plastic water bottles.

_event_location: Miami Watersports: Sailing Center, Rickenbacker Causeway, Key Biscayne, FL
_event_description:
On June 24th from 6:00pm-8:00pm, we will participate in a fun and educational beach and shoreline cleanup hosted by VolunteerCleanup.org.  We’ll help protect our marine environment and Biscayne Bay by removing plastic marine debris while collecting important citizen science data, and compete for the chance to win prizes for whoever finds the strangest thing!

VolunteerCleaunp.org will provide all of the supplies for the cleanup (gloves, bags, pickers, buckets, sunscreen, insect repellent, hand-sanitizer).

Volunteers should:

  • Dress for the weather and wear closed-toed shoes like sneakers and the shoreline is rocky and uneven in some areas.
  • A hat and sunglasses are recommended for a hot and sunny day.
  • Please bring water in your own reusable water bottles. We will have coolers for cold filtered water refills but strongly discourage single-use plastic disposable bottled water.
  • Download the Clean Swell App to participate in the Citizen Science Data Logging. You will work in teams of 2-3.

Breakdown of activities for 2-hour cleanup:

  • Volunteers arrive and check-in (10 min)
  • Introduction and safety briefing (10 min)
  • Explain tasks, distribute supplies (10 min)
  • Shoreline Cleanup, Citizen Science Data logging (1 hour)
  • Regroup at check-in point (30 min)
    • Marine Debris discussion, Q&A, and key takeaways, potential solutions
    • Count and weigh the bags to quantify the impact
    • Take Group Photo
    • Award Contest winners!

Note that the park closes at sundown, which will be at 8:15pm. We will need to make sure we conclude the cleanup promptly at 8pm. If the group arrives late, we will adjust the above schedule as needed. But you should be able to catch a nice view of the sunset from the cleanup location.


Location:

  • The spot does not have an address and has different names depending on who you ask!  So pay attention to these instructions:
  • Use this pin drop of where we will be set up to navigate to the spot: https://maps.app.goo.gl/quSJmxaaA18BhGzd9  
  • It is the FIRST island immediately after you cross the toll plaza from the mainland onto the Rickenbacker causeway.
  • The easiest way to get there is to get into the far right late as soon as you pay the toll plaza and then make the first right into the island.
  • Then, once in the parking lot (the island is basically one big parking lot) go LEFT all the way down to the end and park there. 
  • Once you are in the parking lot, you’ll see the Miami Watersports concessionaire  (you can set GPS to that business as well) and we are past that to the very end of the island.
  • Map is attached where you can see the red arrow where you turn in and the red circle where to park/meet us.
     

**Very important to stay in right lane and DO NOT go over the big Powell Bridge to the next island, otherwise you have to turn around and go all the way back to downtown and through the toll plaza again because there is no left turn to the island from the other direction, only a right hand entrance coming from mainland thru the toll over the causeway.**

_event_title: Miami Waterkeeper Microplastic Marine Debris Cleanup
_event_location: David T. Kennedy Park, South Bayshore Drive, Miami, FL
_event_description:
RSVP ON OUR WEBSITE HERE

Join Miami Waterkeeper for a Microplastic Clean-up at David Kennedy Park!

Microplastics, tiny pieces of plastic less than 5mm in size, pose a significant threat to marine life and coastal ecosystems. Not only will you get to roll up your sleeves and take action, but you'll also learn about the impacts of microplastics and why removing them from our environment is so crucial. So join us at David Kennedy Park and be part of the solution! Together, we can create a cleaner, healthier coastal environment free from the harmful effects of microplastic contamination. Stay tuned for what we plan to do with these microplastics! 

The event starts at 10:00 AM. Please be on time, registration begins 15 minutes before the volunteer workday starts.

Please Bring:

  • Refillable water bottle. Stay hydrated and be prepared to work outside!
  • Closed-toe shoes are required and long-sleeved shirts are and long pants are recommended (clothes that can get wet).
  • A hat, sunblock, and insect repellent (recommended).
  • Gloves you feel comfortable wearing (otherwise Miami Waterkeeper will provide gloves).

RSVP ON OUR WEBSITE HERE
_parking_info: Parking is free

Join the Squad:

_event_location: Morningside Park, Northeast 55th Terrace, Miami, FL
_event_description:
Join SeaKeepers for a coastal cleanup at Morningside Park on Saturday, July 13, 2024! Weather permitting, we will cleanup the whole park including the grass and rocky shoreline. Morningside Park borders Biscayne Bay, and by keeping this park clean we can prevent further pollution to our ocean. Please scroll down and RSVP to join.

Join us by foot or paddle by renting a kayak or SUP from Morningside Watersports at a 30% discount when you say you’re with SeaKeepers. If you would like to paddle out to a nearby picnic island to clean, just ask a SeaKeeper where to go!

In order to participate, all volunteers must complete the required Liability and Appearance Release Waiver HERE.

VOLUNTEER INFORMATION: 

Meeting spot: Look for the blue SeaKeepers branded table and tent next to Morningside Watersports on the left as you enter the park. When you arrive, please scan the QR code or speak to a SeaKeeper to check in. After a brief safety and instructional briefing, we will get you your gear!

Parking: Free parking is available throughout the park, with the closest lot being Lot 7 in front of Morningside Watersports.

Please bring:

Close-toe shoes
Comfortable clothes that may get dirty
Water in a REUSABLE water bottle (no plastic please!)
Sunscreen and bug spray if needed
Hat and sunglasses if wanted


We will provide:

Buckets
Reusable mesh bags
Gloves
Water refills
Community service hours


Marine Debris Tracker: By using the app Marine Debris Tracker, you can log the types of trash you collect and create important data for scientists and lawmakers to better understand the marine debris crisis. This data can lead to legislation such as plastic bans that will keep our ocean cleaner! Make sure to create an account ahead of time and select “The International SeaKeepers Society” as an organization before you start logging. By using the Marine Debris Tracker, you are eligible for 1 extra community service hour. 

For any inquiries or help registering, please contact lillian@seakeepers.org.

We look forward to cleaning with you!

_event_title: 79th Street Neighborhood Cleanup and Business Crawl
_event_location: Shoe Gallery, 1060 Northeast 79th Street, Miami, Florida
_event_description:
Let's take pride in our neighborhood by cleaning it up and supporting local businesses! Did you know that most marine debris (aka ocean trash) originates as street-based or inland litter? By cleaning it up first, we can prevent trash from entering our marine ecosystem and beloved Biscayne Bay.   As we just moved to North Bay Village  (The Heart of the Bay) , we are thrilled to be partnering with some of our fav spots in our new hood for a very fun twist of a cleanup.

GAME PLAN: 

  • We'll kick it off at the Shoe Gallery (free parking onsite)  for introductory remarks, instructions and supply distribution.
  • Then, we'll make our way around the neighorhood cleaning up as we go, stopping for a water break at Technique Records
  • We'll continue the cleanup and then finish it off at The New Schnitzel House for Happy Hour refreshments,  educational debrief and contest winners. 

NEED TO KNOW: 

  • VolunteerCleanup.org will provide all supplies needed for the cleanup (gloves, pickers, buckets, bags, hand-sani, water refills, etc)
  • Community Service Hours provided!
  • Volunteers should wear closed-toed shoes like sneakers, and bring water in a reusable bottle.
  • Pre-signing the online waiver will help expedite check-in! https://forms.gle/1Xx8yk2Ro59avBySA

Join your colleagues for a fun and educational beach cleanup hosted by VolunteerCleanup.org. We’ll help protect our marine environment by removing plastic marine debris while collecting important citizen science data, and compete for the chance to win prizes for whoever finds the strangest thing!   • ATTIRE: Dress for the weather and wear shoes suitable for walking on the beach. We suggest closed-toed shoes like sneakers or water shoes in case of broken glass or jellyfish on the sand.  Hat and sunglasses are also recommended for a hot and sunny day.

  • WAIVERS: Volunteers must check-in and sign waivers before you start. Pre-signing the online waiver will help expedite check-in! https://forms.gle/1Xx8yk2Ro59avBySA
We’ll be meeting at the Osprey Pavilion. Breakdown of activities for 2-hour cleanup: 
  • Volunteers arrive and check-in (10 min)
  • Introduction and safety briefing (10 min)
  • Explain tasks, distribute supplies (10 min)
  • Shoreline Cleanup, Citizen Science Data logging (1 hour)
  • Regroup at check-in point (30 min)Marine Debris discussion, Q&A, and key takeaways, potential solutions
    • Count and weigh the bags to quantify the impact
    • Take Group Photo
    • Award Contest winners!

_event_description:
Ultra Music Festival is back at Bayfront Park for their annual shoreline cleanup!

 

Let’s kick start the season with a shoreline refresh. Come out to cleanup and enjoy music, free Ultra merch and education from the best local non-profits. Participants will have the chance to win two tickets to Ultra Music Festival 2024!

When Ultra Music Festival moved to Virginia Key in 2019, the festival launched its first-ever environmental protection and sustainability campaign ‘Mission: Home.’  The ‘mission’ of the ‘Mission: Home’ program is stated on Ultra’s website as “To preserve our home, reduce our environmental impact and inspire our community to protect the planet.” Since its initial launch in 2019, the program has reached over 6.5 Million people. As that number grows with each passing year, Ultra continues to utilize the power of its platform to spread this inspiring message far beyond the festival grounds.

_event_description:

This will be a guided tour into Biscayne Bay and the mangroves along West Point Preserve on the Northwest side of Key Biscayne, in order to remove marine debris from this vital and hard-to-reach habitat. These types of cleanups are particularly important as mangroves host many vulnerable species and a nursery grounds for species that live within these vital and diverse ecosystems. Our event is funded through a generous grant from the Florida Inland Navigation District. We will have prizes to give away after the cleanup! For the cleanup, you will need to bring your own paddleboard/kayak, and life vest/personal floatation device, we will provide snacks and water. Please see the red circle on the attached map and directions below. Kayak/paddle board rentals:  A limited number of tandem (2-person) kayaks, single person kayaks, and paddleboards will be available for rent from PADL. Click here (link closes at 5:00pm 3/22/2024) to reserve your watercraft if you do not have your own; prices will vary depending on the type of watercraft you choose (tandem kayaks = $60, single kayaks = $40, paddle boards = $40). All PADL rentals include life jacket, whistle, and delivery/pickup at Peacock Park paddlecraft launch. You do not need to change the delivery address, this order link is specific to our cleanup and all watercraft/equipment will all be brought to West Point Preserve launch site. You can specify in the Order Notes “This is for the West Point Preserve cleanup on 3/23/2024.” No refunds can be issued for watercraft rentals for cancellations made after 3/21/2024 or for no-shows on the day of the cleanup. All participants will be provided:

  • reusable gloves,
  • buckets,
  • bags,
  • guidance on the water by a team of experienced local environmentalists.

Participants should wear sun protective clothing and closed-toed shoes that can get wet. Please bring water in a reuseable water bottle and wear reef-safe sunscreen. Children aged 9-17 are welcome as long as they are comfortable and safe being in the water, and are accompanied by a parent or guardian. We can provide Community Service Hours for students upon request, students will get a maxiumum of 3 hours of community service. Questions? Please contact Rumya at 305-361-2770 or rumya@keybiscaynefoundation.org. Ticket sales end at 5:00pm 3/22/2024.

_event_description:
Join Zoom Meeting
https://us06web.zoom.us/j/89915590196?pwd=7CWGDT5jvxhSNot1AX8FUyZHMGPgyR.1

Meeting ID: 899 1559 0196
Passcode: 650202

 

Have you ever wanted to organize a cleanup, but weren't sure where to start? This virtual/zoom workshop is for you! Calling all change-makers, community organizers, neighborhood leaders, student leaders, and any good humans looking to make a difference!! At VolunteerCleanup.org, we've been organizing and leading cleanups for 10+ years and as county organizers for the annual International Coastal Cleanup Day in Miami-Dade we've trained dozens of other groups to lead best in class cleanups that educate and inspire volunteers to be part of the solution. Together, we are building a grassroots movement around the issue of marine debris. Now, we'd like to share what we have learned and what we know, with you-- so you too can start to organize cleanups and collectively we can scale our impact. In this 1-hour workshop you will learn:

  • How to choose a great location
  • How to obtain permission/approval for your cleanup
  • Suggested list of supplies
  • How to post your cleanup on VolunteerCleanup.org and how our website can help you recruit volunteers
  • A suggested breakdown of activities for a 2-hour cleanup
  • How to make your cleanup both productive, fun and educational
  • How to collect citizen science data

*This workshop is made possible by a grant from the City of Miami Beach  Department of Environment and Sustainability. Community service hours provided to all attendees who need one A ZOOM link will be sent via email upon registration.

SPRING EVERGLADES CLEAN-UP 2024
WITH
LOVE THE EVERGLADES MOVEMENT
Saturday, Mar. 9, 2024
2 pm to 6 pm
Love The Everglades Movement is hosting the Spring Everglades Clean-Up 2024!
MEET UP SPOT
We will gather at the Miccosukee Casino & Resort at 2:00 pm.
500 SW 177th Ave, Miami, FL 33194
We will meet at Raccoon 7 - the back portion of the parking lot towards the far right end and then caravan together to the cleanup site.
As the date gets closer, we will post detailed maps and driving info here and on our Instagram stories.
THINGS TO BRING
- Please wear closed-toed shoes that can get dirty or wet
- A Reusable Container for Water
WE PROVIDE
We will supply a water cooler for cold water refills, gloves and garbage bags, but feel free to bring your own work gloves if you have them.
The Everglades Clean-Up is an opportunity for:
- Direct action that brings people into the Everglades;
- Removing garbage and invasive plants.
- Providing education and experiences.
- Community Service.
- Open to All Ages
- Individuals and other organizations to come together and make a difference.
SALVAGE ART
*** As part of this outreach event, we are connecting with artists who wish to use reclaimed materials for artistic sculptures, instruments and other distinctive items.
*** Exhibition and performance presentations details will be forthcoming.
*** If you are an artist who would like to get involved in this aspect of the project please get in touch with us. Thanks!
SIGN UP FOR COMMUNITY HOURS WITH US
As a not-for-profit organization with the State of Florida, Love The Everglades Movement can sign for community hours. If you would like credit for participating in the Spring Everglades Clean-Up 2024, please provide the paperwork required and it will be filled out at the end of the event.
We are happy to provide an outlet for civic engagement and we encourage positive volunteerism on behalf of the Everglades. We appreciate your effort!
A LIL ABOUT US
Love The Everglades Movement (LTEM) is a multi-faceted environmental organization that works to bolster public support for the Everglades with community events. As an organization that utilizes a full spectrum outreach format, LTEM combines education with the arts, spirituality and the inclusion of diverse communities. Our goal is to empower people and provide outlets to protect the Everglades and our natural resources, and to prioritize indigenous environmental priorities.

_event_title: SCOR Love our Oceans Valentine's Day Shoreline Cleanup of the MacArthur Causeway
_event_location: Terminal Island, Miami Beach, FL
_event_description:
Join a group of your colleagues for a fun and educational beach cleanup hosted by VolunteerCleanup.org.  We’ll help protect our marine environment and Biscayne Bay by removing plastic marine debris while collecting important citizen science data, and compete for the chance to win prizes for whoever finds the strangest thing! VolunteerCleaunp.org will provide all of the supplies for the cleanup (gloves, bags, pickers, buckets, sunscreen, insect repellent, hand-sani) Important Reminders for Volunteers:
  • FOOD/DRINK:  Please bring water in your own reusable water bottles. We will have coolers for cold water refills but do not provide plastic disposable bottled water.  The team will head to lunch nearby, following the cleanup
  • ATTIRE: Dress for the weather and wear closed-toed shoes like sneakers as the shoreline is rocky and uneven in some areas. NO flipflops or sandals.  Hat and sunglasses are also recommended for a hot and sunny day.
  • COVID SAFETY:  Follow your company policy.  This will be a socially distanced activity. If you are feeling unwell in any way on the morning of the event, or have had a recent exposure in the days leading up to the cleanup, please stay at home.
  • Download the Clean Swell App to participate in the Citizen Science Data Logging. You will work in teams of 2-3ppl if you came with other guests
  • WAIVERS: Volunteers must check-in and sign waivers before you start. Pre-signing the online waiver will help expedite check-in! https://forms.gle/1Xx8yk2Ro59avBySA
Breakdown of activities for 2-hour cleanup:
  • Volunteers arrive and check-in (10 min)
  • Introduction and safety briefing (10 min)
  • Explain tasks, distribute supplies (10 min)
  • Shoreline Cleanup, Citizen Science Data logging (1 hour)
  • Regroup at check-in point (30 min)Marine Debris discussion, Q&A, and key takeaways, potential solutions
    • Count and weigh the bags to quantify the impact
    • Take Group Photo
    • Award Contest winners!

_event_title: West Point Preserve Mangrove Paddle Cleanup
_event_location: West Point Preserve, Key Biscayne, FL
_event_description:
THIS CLEANUP HAS BEEN POSTPONED DUE TO INCLEMENT WEATHER.  IT HAS BEEN RESCHEDULED FOR MARCH 23, 2024.  CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE NEW DATE.

 

Join Key Biscayne Community Foundation’s Citizen Science Program, FillABag, Miami EcoAdventures, and Free Plastic for an impactful and unforgettable mangrove cleanup out of West Point Preserve in Key Biscayne! This will be a guided tour into Biscayne Bay and the mangroves along West Point Preserve on the Northwest side of Key Biscayne, in order to remove marine debris from this vital and hard-to-reach habitat. These types of cleanups are particularly important as mangroves host many vulnerable species and a nursery grounds for species that live within these vital and diverse ecosystems.

Our event is funded through a generous grant from the Florida Inland Navigation District. We will have prizes to give away after the cleanup! For the cleanup, you will need to bring your own paddleboard/kayak, and life vest/personal floatation device, we will provide snacks and water. Parking will be in the back lot behind the Crossbridge (Presbyterian) Church at 160 Harbor Drive (just past the Presbyterian school heading south). Please see the red circle on the attached map and directions below.

Kayak/paddle board rentals:  A limited number of tandem (2-person) kayaks, single person kayaks, and paddleboards will be available for rent from PADL. Click here (link closes at 5:00pm 2/17/2024) to reserve your watercraft if you do not have your own; prices will vary depending on the type of watercraft you choose (tandem kayaks = $60, single kayaks = $40, paddle boards = $40). All PADL rentals include life jacket, whistle, and delivery/pickup at Peacock Park paddlecraft launch. You do not need to change the delivery address, this order link is specific to our cleanup and all watercraft/equipment will all be brought to West Point Preserve launch site. You can specify in the Order Notes “This is for the West Point Preserve cleanup on 2/18/2024.” No refunds can be issued for watercraft rentals for cancellations made after 2/16/2024 or for no-shows on the day of the cleanup. All participants will be provided:

  • reusable gloves,
  • buckets,
  • bags,
  • guidance on the water by a team of experienced local environmentalists.

 

Participants should wear sun protective clothing and closed-toed shoes that can get wet. Please bring water in a reuseable water bottle and wear reef-safe sunscreen. Children aged 9-17 are welcome as long as they are comfortable and safe being in the water, and are accompanied by a parent or guardian. We can provide Community Service Hours for students upon request, students will get a maxiumum of 3 hours of community service. Questions? Please contact Rumya at 305-361-2770 or rumya@keybiscaynefoundation.org. Ticket sales end at 5:00pm 2/17/2024.

_event_description:
Join Key Biscayne Community Foundation’s Citizen Science Program, FillABag, Miami EcoAdventures, and Free Plastic for an impactful and unforgettable mangrove cleanup out of Peacock Park in Coconut Grove! This will be a guided tour into Biscayne Bay and the mangroves on Dinner Key, where we can also get off our paddleboards and walk around to remove marine debris from this vital and hard-to-reach habitat. These types of cleanups are particularly important as mangroves host many vulnerable species that live within these vital and diverse ecosystems. Our event is funded through a generous grant from the Florida Inland Navigation District. We will have prizes to give away after the cleanup!

For the cleanup, you will need to bring your own paddleboard/kayak, and life vest/personal floatation device, we will provide snacks and water. CLICK ON THE MAP BELOW TO SEE WHERE YOU SHOULD PARK AND WHERE YOU WILL NEED TO WALK TO THE LAUNCH SITE.

Kayak/paddle board rentals:  A limited number of tandem (2-person) kayaks, single person kayaks, and paddleboards will be available for rent from PADL. Click here (this link closes at 5:00pm 1/20/2024) to reserve your watercraft if you do not have your own; prices will vary depending on the type of watercraft you choose (tandem kayaks = $60, single kayaks = $40, paddle boards = $40). All PADL rentals include life jacket, whistle, and delivery/pickup at Peacock Park paddlecraft launch. You do not need to change the delivery address, this order link is specific to our cleanup and all watercraft/equipment will all be brought to Peacock Park paddlecraft launch. You can specify in the Order Notes “This is for the Peacock Park cleanup on 1/21/2024.” No refunds can be issued for watercraft rentals for cancellations made after 1/19/2024 or for no-shows on the day of the cleanup.

All participants will be provided:

  • reusable gloves,
  • buckets,
  • bags,
  • guidance on the water by a team of experienced local environmentalists. 

 

Participants should wear sun protective clothing and closed-toed shoes that can get wet. Please bring water in a reuseable water bottle and wear reef-safe sunscreen. Children aged 9-17 are welcome as long as they are comfortable and safe being in the water, and are accompanied by a parent or guardian. We can provide Community Service Hours for students upon request, students will get a maxiumum of 3 hours of community service. Questions? Please contact Rumya at 305-361-2770 or rumya@keybiscaynefoundation.org. Ticket sales end at 7:00pm 1/20/2024.
