_event_description:
Join a group of your colleagues for a fun and educational beach cleanup hosted by VolunteerCleanup.org, in honor of MLK Day of Service. 

We’ll help protect our marine environment by removing plastic marine debris while collecting important citizen science data, and compete for the chance to win prizes for whoever finds the strangest thing!

VolunteerCleaunp.org will provide all of the supplies for the cleanup (gloves, bags, pickers, buckets, sunscreen, insect repellent, hand-sani) 

COMMUNITY SERVICE HOURS PROVIDED! 

We’ll be meeting at Pelican Pavilion, which you can access from Parking Lot #5

Important Reminders for Volunteers:

  • FOOD/DRINK:  Please bring water in your own reusable water bottles. We will have coolers for cold water refills but do not provide plastic disposable bottled water.
  • ATTIRE: Dress for the weather and wear shoes suitable for walking on the beach. We suggest closed-toed shoes like sneakers or water shoes in case of broken glass or jellyfish on the sand.  Hat and sunglasses are also recommended for a hot and sunny day.
  • COVID SAFETY:  Follow your company policy.  This will be a socially distanced activity. If you are feeling unwell in any way on the morning of the event, or have had a recent exposure in the days leading up to the cleanup, please stay at home.
  • Download the Clean Swell App to participate in the Citizen Science Data Logging. You will work in teams of 2-3ppl if you came with other guests
  • WAIVERS: Volunteers must check-in and sign waivers before you start. Pre-signing the online waiver will help expedite check-in! https://forms.gle/1Xx8yk2Ro59avBySA
     

Breakdown of activities for 2-hour cleanup: 

  • Volunteers arrive and check-in (10 min)
  • Introduction and safety briefing (10 min)
  • Explain tasks, distribute supplies (10 min)
  • Shoreline Cleanup, Citizen Science Data logging (1 hour)
  • Regroup at check-in point (30 min)Marine Debris discussion, Q&A, and key takeaways, potential solutions
  • Count and weigh the bags to quantify the impact
  • Take Group Photo
  • Award Contest winners!

_event_description:
Come on out and join us for our New Years Day beach cleanup! Please bring along sunscreen, insect repellent, and a reusable water bottle.  We will provide buckets, trash bags, and trash grabbers. Gear and guidance will be available during this cleanup for those interested in sand sifting for microplastics.

We meet at Pavilion C-16 beach access 7 near the lighthouse. The Cleanup lasts from 9am to 11am. Expect a long line to enter the park. When you arrive to the park tell the ranger on duty that you are attending the beach cleanup and they will give you directions and waive the entrance fee.

Individuals under 18 years of age require adult supervision.  Please, no drop-offs.   

This is a great way to earn volunteer hours for school or work, so please tell your friends about this opportunity.  All Volunteers will receive a letter certifying their volunteer hours.

Thank you and we hope to see you there.  We believe that teaching stewardship for our environment and community is the best hope for the future of our parks.

_event_location: Biscayne National Park, 9700 Southwest 328th Street, Homestead, FL
_event_description:
Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Day of Service at Biscayne National Park

Come out and experience your national park!

Note: *individual* participant must be age 18 and over-no minors will be permitted to participate.

Meet time is at 8:00am, Saturday, January 27th at the Dante Fascell Visitor Center at Biscayne National Park. The address is: 

9700 SW 328th Street, Homestead, FL 33030

 What we will be doing:

We will boat across Biscayne Bay (~45 minutes) to the oceanside of Elliott Key. Will anchor in waist-deep water and wade onto the beach. We will perform marine debris removal. You must be comfortable with wading in knee-deep water on soft, mucky bottom.  Once done, we will take photos, weigh the bags of trash, and load the boat. We will dispose of our debris upon our return to Headquarters. Site selection will depend upon weather & water conditions. 

We will provide: 

Life jackets, data sheets, trash bags, bug spray, sunscreen, first-aid kit, gloves for hand protection (however, these are a one-size-fits-all deal, so if you have your own that you prefer, like garden or work gloves, please feel free to bring those), trash grabbers, your own trash collection buckets if you so desire.

Please bring: 

Close-toed shoes that can get wet are mandatory-this is a safety requirement. (dive booties are recommended), bathing suit, clothing that can get wet. Hat, sunglasses, water jugs and water bottles (bring already full if possible), snacks if you want. 

For more information, contact Ana Zangroniz at: azangroniz@ufl.edu. 

This event is to honor the legacy and memory of Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. This event is a partnership between Biscayne National Park and the Florida Sea Grant Extension Program in Miami-Dade County.

_parking_info: Plenty of free parking available on site.

To continue to drive further impact additional events have been confirmed for LA, San Francisco and Miami, and we’re just getting started!

Our Partners

The 501c3 non-profit builds tools, mobilizes communities, and develops educational resources and standards that inspire global action and catalyze cross-sector change.
For more information about this event or to learn more about OG, visit oceanic.global or follow Oceanic Global on Instagram @oceanic.global.

    • Award Contest winners!

_event_description:
Come join SeaKeepers for our monthly cleanup at Morningside Park! Weather permitting, we will cleanup all along the waterside with the option to kayak or paddleboard to the nearby Picnic Islands. Make sure to visit the SeaKeepers tent for check-in, and then instructions and a safety-briefing will be given to the group!
You are welcome to join us on foot or by paddle! SeaKeepers will NOT be providing kayaks. You may bring your own kayak or paddleboard, or kayak and paddleboard rentals are available from Morningside Watersports at a 30% discount when you mention you’re with SeaKeepers! You will be able to paddle across Biscayne Bay to the nearby Picnic Islands to clean up there as well. A SeaKeeper will show you where to go! 
FOR CHECK-IN:
For contact-less check-in, bring your smart phone to the event. 
IN ORDER TO PARTICIPATE YOU MUST COMPLETE A LIABILITY WAIVER HERE. You will not be allowed to participate without this form signed. Please do this when you RSVP/sign up so we can save time for cleaning on the day of the event!
Recycling is encouraged! We would love for you to separate out any aluminum cans, glass bottles or plastic bottles that you find, as these are all accepted materials.   
Supplies you can bring:
🦈 Reusable water bottle with water (no single-use plastic bottles!)
🦈 Reef-safe Sunscreen (make sure oxybenzone is NOT on the active ingredients list!)
🦈 Comfortable shoes
🦈 Download the app Marine Debris Tracker, and click here for a quick tutorial on how to use the app, and get ready to utilize the Marine Debris Tracker App to help create a bigger picture of marine debris and plastic pollution through collecting open data, generating scientific findings, informing policy, and inspiring upstream design.
*You can earn extra community service hours by participating!
🦈 Follow and monitor our Instagram page, @seakeepers for updates!  
We will provide:
🦈 Garbage bags 
🦈 Reusable gloves
🦈 Hand Sanitizer
🦈 Extra water
🦈 Community Service Hours / Service Learning Hours
Please note, the cleanup is 2 hours long, so that is how many hours we will give for community service. However, if you use the Marine Debris Tracker to record trash data, we will give you FIVE hours!
Marine debris isn’t an ocean problem – it’s a people problem. Be part of the solution!
 
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:
Parking: Park in lot 7 (the first lot on your left as you enter, or the last lot on your right as you exit) near the kayak launch. 
Cancellation or Postponing:
Cleanup will proceed as scheduled rain or shine, and cleanups will only be affected by the presence of lightning. Any extreme or hazardous weather will be monitored closely and the final call will be made to cancel or postpone a cleanup 2 hours prior to the start of the cleanup. For example, a 9am cleanup that is being postponed due to weather will be cancelled at 7am. Volunteers will be notified by email.
_meeting_spot_details: Look for our blue SeaKeepers branded tent next to Morningside Watersports
_parking_info: Park in lot 7 (the first lot on your left as you enter, or the last lot on your right as you exit) near the kayak launch.

Join a group of your colleagues for a fun and educational beach cleanup hosted by VolunteerCleanup.org.  We’ll help protect our marine environment by removing plastic marine debris while collecting important citizen science data, and compete for the chance to win prizes for whoever finds the strangest thing!     • Take Group Photo
    • Award Contest winners!

_event_location: Biscayne National Park, 9700 Southwest 328th Street, Homestead, Florida 33033
_event_description:
Thank you for your interest in keeping Biscayne beautiful!

 

We offer free and fun beach cleanups for pre-organized groups of 4-12 volunteers (ages 16 and up) on weekdays of your choice from December through April. The journey begins at our visitor center in Homestead, FL and will be from 8am to 3pm. The cleanups including taking park boats across the bay to the oceanside of our barrier islands to clean our sea turtle nesting beaches if the weather is nice. 

 

This volunteer experience is best suited for volunteers with a moderate to high level of physical fitness and balance. Work includes wading in waist deep water, walking over sharp rocks and/or through mucky sediment, bending down and lifting heavy objects, prolonged standing on moving boats, getting in and out of boats from waist deep water, working in buggy conditions, heat, and sun for 5+ hours and will be strenuous. 

 

If this is of interest to you and your group, email Bisc_Beach_Cleanup@nps.gov

_event_title: Reverse Tashlich-Indian Creek Waterway Clean Up
_event_location: Miami Beach JCC, 4221 Pine Tree Drive, Miami Beach, FL
_event_description:
Please join us on Sunday, September, 10, 9:00 for a family friendly, morning program on the Miami Beach  JCC Sol Stern Dock as we use the kayaks and canoes of the Mariner Program to help keep the Indian Creek Waterway clean in a pre-High Holiday - Reverse Tashlich!

Bring all your friends!  This event is open to all ages (Parents must accompany children under 14). Community Service hours given.

The event is free but a donation of $18 is suggested to support Clean Miami Beach a non-profit dedicated to clean beaches, water and ending single use plastics. They will be on hand to assist with nets, grabbers, buckets and other equipment.

MBJCC Lifeguards will be present. Refreshments will be served!

Go to  https://mbjcc.ticketleap.com/reverse-tashlich/ to RSVP!

We would love to see you there. Everyone is welcome!

What is a Reverse Tashlich?

Sponsored by the Jewish organization Tikkun HaYam-Repair the Sea, the Reverse Tashlich program, conducted worldwide, reimagines the High Holiday Tashlich ceremony of symbolically casting away sins into water. The symbolism is reversed: participants come together to clean up waterways that impact our lives, fostering a spiritual connection to and stewardship for the environment.

See you then!

_event_location: U.S. 1 & Riviera Drive, Coral Gables, FL
_event_description:
Hi Volunteers!!! Thank you for participating in this years International Coastal Cleanup!  I wanted to share a few details with you guys! Thank you for signing up to volunteer for International Coastal Cleanup Miami-Dade on Saturday, September 16th from 9am until noon.  This event will be held at the Coral Gables Launch Site located on Riviera Drive and US1. This cleanup would be on land but also on our Coral Gables Waterway.  We do encourage volunteers and residents to bring their own paddle boards and kayaks if you would like to participate on the waterway portion of our cleanup! We will have our checkin table with Lucy Lopez, Matt Anderson and Solanch Lopez at the launch site located on US1 and Riviera Drive.  There will be no parking allowed on the actual launch site only to launch your kayak, paddle board or canoe.  Free parking is available at 4600 Ponce de Leon and its less than a 5 minute walk. This is a pretty busy street.  Please use caution if needing to cross the street. Keep Coral Gables Beautiful has donated safety vests for all participants, please wear these while picking up trash. After you pick up, please bring the bags back to the check in table and place near the trash bin, not inside. A few important reminders: 
  • Complete the online waiver here: https://forms.gle/fj1DmQhWW4xts25f9  **If you are under 18 and coming without a parent or guardian, you must have a parent/guardian sign the waiver in advance. https://forms.gle/fj1DmQhWW4xts25f9
  • Wear: Dress for the weather, wear appropriate footwear. Closed-toed shoes (like sneakers or water shoes that you don’t mind getting dirty) are suggested
  • Please bring water in a reusable bottle to reduce single-use plastic waste.
  • Download the Clean Swell App:  You will be working in teams of 2-3 collecting Citizen Science data using provided paper data cards or the Clean Swell mobile app. Download the free app from your app store in advance if you would like to use it instead of the card. If you have a smart phone, it’s more fun and easier to use the app!   https://oceanconservancy.org/trash-free-seas/international-coastal-cleanup/cleanswell/  Data collection is required for students who need community service hours.
  • Gloves:  If you have your own work/garden or dishwashing gloves, please bring them. We will have reusable working gloves on hand, but cannot guarantee having your size. Those with very small or very large hands may want to bring their own.
  • Buckets:  Some volunteers find it convenient to use a bucket while doing a cleanup and it also help us to consolidate the trash into fewer plastic trash bags. You can repurpose free buckets from many local restaurants. Try asking your local Chinese restaurant, fast food burger place or donut shop as they often get food items delivered in 5-gallon buckets and are usually happy to give them away to volunteers. Repurposing Smaller kitty litter buckets make great buckets for younger kids at cleanups too!
  • Community Service Hours:  Bring your own paperwork if you need it signed from us, otherwise, if you need our certificates, kindly let me know so we can be sure to have enough forms on hand.
  • **Please DO NOT attend the activity if you’ve had a recent COVID-19 exposure, have any cold or flu-like symptoms, or are feeling unwell in any way on the day of the event.
Spearheaded globally by the Ocean Conservancy, VolunteerCleanup.org organizes Miami-Dade’s local participation in this annual event with 50+ simultaneous shoreline cleanups around the county and is made possible by the generous support of our presenting sponsors Covanta and Boucher Brothers, with additional support from Blackstone Charitable Foundation, The Brady Hunter Foundation, Benjamin & Gloria Joannou, Jr. Family Conservation Fund, City of Miami Beach, The Miami Foundation, Loud And Live, and Miami-Dade County RER-DERM   Thank you for volunteering. Looking forward to a great impactful day!

Volunteers should not lift anything too heavy – when in doubt, don’t try! Always notify a Site Captain of this type of debris for further assistance. - Do not go near any suspected hazardous materials (e.g., propane tanks, oil or chemical drums, etc.). If debris is spotted that a volunteer suspects to be hazardous or potentially hazardous, the debris should be left untouched and the site should be immediately informed. The local fire/hazmat department, environmental health agency or the Coast Guard National Response Center should be notified and respond as appropriate. - While it is highly unlikely that marine debris will be radioactive and hazardous, and although marine debris items such as drums or chemical canisters are uncommon, it is important that marine debris that is suspected as being hazardous be assessed and removed by trained professionals who can ensure the public’s safety. Help keep this historic initiative on track ... Invite your friends and sign-up today!!!

_event_description: In conjunction with the International Coastal Cleanup, please join us at Coconut Grove Sailing Club for the next Clarington Island Cleanup on Saturday, September 16th! Wear closed toed shoes, bring your own sunblock and a reusable water bottle. We shall supply gloves, bags for garbage and a light lunch after we finish. Children 12 and older may participate, and community service certificates are available for students. YOU MUST REGISTER HERE to participate, and each volunteer must have a separate registration. Park either on the McFarlane Road outside the gate or in a public garage, as parking in the lot CGSC is reserved for members only. All are welcome!
